items.text: What if every hard session your child just finished was teaching their nervous system to be slower?
items.notes: From direct document extraction (no brief code; sequential assigned)

items.text: The program that looked hardest got the worst results. Every single time.
Your child isn't behind. Their training system is — and there's a measurable reason why.
There's a moment in every set when it stops being training and starts being anti-training. No program in this market knows when that moment happens.
Your kid hasn't been failing. The training system has been flying blind.
Every coach says 'two more' at the end of every drill. Here's what those last two reps are actually doing to your athlete's speed.
The reps that are making your kid slower are the ones every coach calls the most important.
Your athlete shows up. Works hard. Never quits. And hasn't gotten faster in six months. Here's the reason — and it's not them.
Nobody in youth sports will say this out loud: those last reps when your kid slows down are teaching their body to move slowly.
Your kid's training is working perfectly. The problem is what it's teaching.
The window they told you to wait for? It closes before puberty starts.
I've used this same technology to help build a 7× Pro Bowl offensive lineman. I'm now using it on 9-year-olds. The science is the same. The window of opportunity is better.
Speed isn't born. It's a movement pattern your nervous system learns — or doesn't.
We measure your child's explosive output to the hundredth of a meter per second. Every rep.
For 8–12 year old athletes who work hard but aren't getting faster.
Hamilton County parents: the developmental window for speed is open. It closes at puberty.
There's no middle ground. Either you are all in and get private training just to be able to keep up... or you fall back into rec.

items.text: Which of these common youth speed training drills has been shown to make athletes SLOWER — the longer the drill goes on?
